name: Hungary 1950–56 (Golden Team)
scopeNote: Hungary national team, 1950–1956 (Golden Team), under Gusztáv Sebes (in charge from 1949). Unbeaten run from June 1950 to the 1954 World Cup final (Wikipedia: 'unbeaten in their last 32 matches' before the final, lost 3–2 to West Germany on 1954-07-04). Start day and end day not found: start is month-only (first unbeaten match not located), end is year-only (the end of the era, linked to 1956, not pinned to a day). Key matches: 1952 Helsinki Olympics gold, Wembley 6–3 on 1953-11-25, World Cup 1954 quarter-final v Brazil 4–2 (1954-06-27), semi-final v Uruguay 4–2 (1954-06-30). Named style: 'a deep-lying centre forward who pulled defenders out of position' (guidetofootball.com), i.e. Hidegkuti as a withdrawn centre-forward. Wikipedia names the shape 'an extremely flexible 3–2–3–2 formation' that 'eventually evolv[ed] into the 4–2–4 formation'. The 4–2–4 label is therefore disputed for this era, not verified for it. Tactical evidence is retrospective (Wikipedia, guidetofootball) plus one tier B source (These Football Times) with a few dated match facts; no period tactical analysis was read.
openQuestions: Formation conflict: Wikipedia says 3–2–3–2 evolving into 4–2–4; guidetofootball contrasts the side with the W-M formation without naming a formation. Decide whether this profile is the 4–2–4 exemplar, as the ideology file says, or 3–2–3–2 with 4–2–4 as later evolution.
Start day (first unbeaten match, June 1950) and end day (1956) are not verified: check before the audit if a day is needed.

Marking: no source read says whether Hungary marked zonally or man-oriented. The only verified evidence is that centre-halves who marked the centre-forward followed Hidegkuti into midfield (Wikipedia, guidetofootball). Wembley 1953 (Johnston drawn out of position) comes from a search summary only, not verified.

Sebes's stated view on tactics was not found: no dated primary interview. The only Sebes quote found (TFT, 'The bitter struggle between capitalism and communism...') is undated and unsourced, so not saved as statedView.
Quotes in this file were extracted by the page-reading tool and checked against its summaries, not copied by hand: spot-check the quotes against the pages before the audit.

Pressing, set pieces, build-up and squad building: no verified fact found. People management and Sebes's dressing-room relationships (e.g. Grosics: 'made a political issue of every important match') are undated and were not saved as facts.

sources.title: Magical Magyars (Guide to Football, history)
sources.evidence: "playing its centre forward, Nándor Hidegkuti, much deeper than usual"; the team's innovation summarised as "a deep-lying centre forward who pulled defenders out of position". Describes the W-M formation as the common alternative; does not name Hungary's own formation.

sources.title: Magical Magyars (Guide to Football, history)
sources.evidence: "If he followed Hidegkuti into midfield, he opened space behind for the inside forwards to attack." Describes the opposing centre-back's dilemma; does not describe Hungary's own marking.

sources.title: Magical Magyars (Guide to Football, history)
sources.evidence: "The wingers tucked in to support the inside forwards." Retrospective account; the page does not mention full-backs.

sources.title: Magical Magyars (Guide to Football, history)
sources.evidence: Bozsik, a half-back, "often pushed forward into the spaces vacated by Hidegkuti". Read through the page-reading tool, not copied verbatim: spot-check before relying on it.

sources.title: Gusztáv Sebes: the pioneering brain behind Hungary's Magical Magyars (These Football Times)
sources.evidence: Before the 1953 match at Wembley, Sebes gave a four-hour tactical talk, and the squad trained with the heavier ball used in England. Article text read through the page-reading tool; spot-check the wording.

sources.title: Gusztáv Sebes: the pioneering brain behind Hungary's Magical Magyars (These Football Times)
sources.evidence: Ahead of internationals Sebes arranged warm-up games against local club sides and had them adopt the tactics of the upcoming opponent. No date given for the practice; period not pinned.

sources.title: Gusztáv Sebes: the pioneering brain behind Hungary's Magical Magyars (These Football Times)
sources.evidence: Hidegkuti moved to outside left for the 1954 World Cup semi-final against Uruguay (4–2, 1954-06-30, confirmed on the Golden Team page). Sebes was criticised after the 1954 final for selecting Tóth on the left and Czibor on the right.

sources.title: Match of the Century, England v Hungary 1953 (Wikipedia, via search summary only)
sources.evidence: Search summary only, not read: England centre-half Harry Johnston was pulled out of position by the deep-lying Hidegkuti. Not verified.

confidence.reason: Mostly tier C retrospectives (Wikipedia, Guide to Football) plus one tier B source; all tactical facts are retrospective, with no period quote. Formation disputed (3–2–3–2 per Wikipedia vs 4–2–4). Marking, pressing, Sebes's stated view and most dimensions unverified.
